column1: # The shard table. THE one place a shard's identity lives; bash and Python both read this file.
# A "domain" to the router (src/retrieval/shard_router.py) is a CPC SUBCLASS, four characters, plus
# the literal "unclassified" that route() always emits. There are 602 of those and eight shards, so
# a shard owns an explicit SET of subclasses and the mapping subclass -> shard is by exact match.
# THE ASSIGNMENT IS NOT OURS. It is workstream F's balanced eight way partition, computed once and
# written to its data/logs/plan.json. `ops/shards/plan_to_table.py --plan <plan.json>` regenerates
# the last column from it and `--check` fails if this file has drifted. Do not hand edit the domain
# lists: a subclass F loaded onto one shard and this table routes to another is a shard that wakes,
# is queried and answers nothing, which downstream is indistinguishable from a genuine miss.
# domain_08 carries the `*` catch-all AND the `unclassified` route, which is 1,024,320 publications,
# 20.6% of the corpus, that no classified shard holds. A symbol the plan has never seen and a
# document with no symbol at all are the same problem, so they live on the same box.
# `shard_of("")` and `shard_of(shard_router.UNCLASSIFIED)` both land here: workstream B's
# corpus_niche.subclass_of returns "" where domain_of returns "unclassified", and a shard reachable
# under only one of the two names is 20.6% of the corpus quietly unreachable.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   shard    shard id, F's own key for the domain group. Also the lease key in `shard_leases`.
#   vm       the instance name
#   zone     the instance zone
#   domains  comma separated CPC subclasses this shard owns, `*` first on the catch-all
# THE FLEET IS SPREAD OVER THREE ZONES ON PURPOSE: three in us-central1-a, three in -c, two in -f.
# MEASURED 2026-08-22, over ninety minutes: `instances.create` AND `instances.start` for a
# c4-highmem-16 in us-central1-b return ZONE_RESOURCE_POOL_EXHAUSTED_WITH_DETAILS on ten separate
# attempts, while -a, -c and -f succeeded first try every time and GCE's own error names those
# three as having capacity. A TERMINATED VM holds NO capacity reservation, so this is not a build
# time problem: it is the cold tier's steady state failure mode, and a shard in a zone that cannot
# start it contributes nothing on every search.
# So: no shard in us-central1-b, and no zone holding more than three of the eight. All eight in
# one zone would mean one stockout takes the WHOLE cold tier out at once; spread, a stockout costs
# the shards in that zone and the tier answers with the rest, which is what it is designed to do.
# The zone is a per shard column for exactly this reason. If -b recovers it is a fine place for a
# shard again; move one back by editing this column and recreating that VM, since a disk is zonal.
# Cross zone inside a region is internal IP traffic at about a third of a millisecond extra, and a
# shard answers with (publication_id, score) rows, tens of kilobytes. It is not a latency argument.
# All eight exist. `shardctl.sh status` is the live picture; `shardctl.sh cost` is the arithmetic.
# A shard's resting state is TERMINATED and the idle reaper is what keeps it that way.
